title: Raman spectroscopy of the van der Waals altermagnet Co$_{1/4}$NbSe$_2$
authors: Dushyanthini Balasundaram, Bishal Thapa, Resham Regmi, Nirmal J. Ghimire, Igor I. Mazin, Patrick M. Vora
abstract: We investigate the influence of Co intercalation and altermagnetic order on the lattice dynamics of the layered compound Co$_{1/4}$NbSe$_2$. Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy, supported by density-functional theory, enables identification of six Raman-active phonons. Co intercalation drives a substantial reconstruction of the vibrational spectrum through zone folding of NbSe$_2$ phonons, producing hybridized modes with mixed zone-center and zone-boundary character. Despite this, Co atoms do not participate in any Raman-active modes by symmetry, which is in marked contrast to related 1/3 compounds where intercalant modes do contribute to the Raman spectrum. Temperature-dependent Raman measurements across the altermagnetic transition show no discontinuities, which is consistent with short-range spin correlations in the quasi-one-dimensional Co chains. However, we find evidence for spin-phonon coupling in A$_{1g}$ symmetry modes owing to their out-of-plane Se displacements. Our work demonstrates the substantial impact of intercalation on the vibrational properties of transition metal dichalcogenides and the presence of spin-phonon interactions in a newly discovered altermagnetic material.
summary: The study uses advanced Raman spectroscopy and DFT calculations to characterize the vibrational properties of the altermagnetic material $	ext{Co}_{1/4}	ext{NbSe}_2$. It reveals that Co intercalation reconstructs the phonon spectrum while confirming the existence of spin-phonon coupling in specific modes. This work advances understanding of how magnetic ordering influences lattice dynamics in transition metal dichalcogenides.
main_problem: The study investigates how Co intercalation and altermagnetic ordering affect the lattice dynamics of the layered van der Waals material $	ext{Co}_{1/4}	ext{NbSe}_2$. The goal is to identify vibrational signatures and evidence for spin-phonon coupling.
main_result: Intercalation causes significant reconstruction of the phonon spectrum via zone folding, while temperature measurements reveal indirect spin-phonon coupling in specific $	ext{A}_{1g}$ symmetry modes. Furthermore, Co atoms do not contribute to any Raman-active modes by symmetry.
method: The research combines polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations to model phonon dispersion and analyze temperature dependence across the altermagnetic transition.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Co}_{1/4}	ext{NbSe}_2$, an altermagnet, which is a layered van der Waals material. The analysis models lattice vibrations using DFT for various magnetic states (NM, FM, AFM) and examines temperature evolution via the Balkanski anharmonic model.
key_observables: Raman-active phonon frequencies ($	ext{cm}^{-1}$), mode symmetry ($	ext{A}_{1g}, 	ext{E}_{2g}$, etc.), spectral weight changes due to zone folding, and spin-phonon coupling constants ($\lambda$).
important_parameters: Altermagnetic transition temperature ($T_N \approx 168 	ext{ K}$), magnetic moment ($\mu_B$), and the coupling constant $\lambda$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that spin-phonon coupling can be quantified by analyzing frequency shifts ($\Delta\omega$) relative to zero-temperature fits, despite the itinerant nature of Co electrons.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate lattice structures, polarization-resolved Raman spectra showing selection rules, and temperature evolution plots demonstrating phonon frequency shifts across multiple samples.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents structural details, analyzes the spectral reconstruction due to intercalation using DFT calculations for various symmetry modes, examines temperature dependence relative to $T_N$, and finally quantifies spin-phonon coupling constants ($\lambda$) based on mode eigenvectors.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed spectroscopic probe into emergent magnetic phenomena (altermagnetism) in 2D materials, linking electronic order directly to lattice vibrations via measurable Raman shifts. This type of magneto-vibrational coupling is highly relevant for designing novel quantum materials.
